searchText: How often would zero-gas tx occur pre-1559? [context: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4803] Would Flashbots bundles generally pay out-of-band, for instance? <@!339771292884664320> yes, and miner payouts would pay 0 gas too I'm not sure if a 0 gas txn would actually get propagated on the p2p network, but if you could send it to a miner and one way or another get them to include it, it would be valid. https://gist.github.com/axic/b5f2f27f4eb342fd0eb5539aa92fce15 for the interested I think going with contract massively reduces complexity, regardless of how the CL ETH is transported back into EL Fight in #party-lounge my pref is irregular state change at shanghai that deploys the bytecode and drops in `2^42069` into the contract my second pref is irregular state change at shanghai that deploys the bytecode and adds an exceptional rule for sending regardless of blaance of that contract I can't really join the breakout room today, but I would go towards your second pref. Re withdrawals. I would like to also rectify the total supply problem. Potentially at the beginning of a block both the withdrawal and deposit contracts balances could be synchronised according to the beacon state. very interesting discussion, i hope we will get back to it sometime soon. but gotta drop off 👋 Does that imply that withdrawals need to be done at the start of the block? No Ah, so during a block’s execution, you end up with different balances, but it resets each block? yes i dont think it is cosmetic, but rather removing the need for precompiles and or special transfer rules initially i was like "lets replace the deposit contract code" to have withdrawals, but i think setting at the block is nicer / less riskier Is there a way to do this with "perfect" accounting, e.g. at a transaction level rather than block? I feel we should at least consider the option before we dismiss it as being too complex. basically balances over execution+consensus are 100% correct at the beginning of the block, so if anyone needs that figure they need to check it at the beginning not sure the complexity to do it at tx level is worth it I think it will be correct for the entire block. i think so too, but havent verified my assumption People can use `SELFDESTRUCT` to send eth to the withdrawal contract. AH! I just realized I had misunderstood your proposal, Alex. You are saying that, at the start of the block you deduct from the deposit contract the sum of all the withdrawal receipts which will be processed in this block? You just set the deposit contract to 0. And you set the withdraw contract to the "balance of consensus layer ETH". ☝️ Ahhh! That means that you are then bringing in the validator rewards in the EL, correct? (accounting-wise) could also set deposit to `balance - pending_withdraw`, and withdrawal to `pending_withdraw` I prefer this, but both options are much simpler/cleaner than what I had in mind 😄 if we want to make it more complicated :) This might also make it easier to test for edge cases, right, because we'd expect the withdrawal contract to end the block at >0, but close, rather than `balance-pending_withdraw` https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/how-the-potato-changed-the-world-108470605/ I'm under the impression that potatos caused Maori warfare to be far more damaging, since expeditions could last longer. It didn't help that firearms were introduced at the same time. this conversation has evolved in an interesting direction https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sKjHvpiHk3s Gtg, cya https://www.effectivealtruism.org/ https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Man_Who_Knew_Infinity Let us know when you are back and fixed <@!199561711278227457>. omg, the call is still on? did a walk on the coast, survived a blizzard, and I get back to seeing the call being on?! <@!243183686562873344> You should fix the formatting on that EIP: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4747#abstract I think just the hiding block is not working with quotes Thanks for the great chat! `30000000*1.0009765625^x=2^31-1` https://github.com/ethereumjs/rustbn.js ```rust use std::os::raw::c_char; #[cfg(native)] extern "C" { fn call_func(name: *const c_char, inputs: *const [u8; 32], outputs: *mut [u8; 32]); } ```
